title: p-block elements (groups 13–18)
group: CHEM-ATOM / CHEM-PER — Atoms & the Periodic Table
examples: What are the general properties of the p-block elements?
How does electronegativity change across a period in the p-block?
Can you give an example of an oxoacid from the p-block?

explain.say: Today we explore the p-block elements on the periodic table.
The first trend we look at is electronegativity across a period.
Next we consider the general trend in acidity of oxoacids.
We look at important compounds like the halides of Group 17 elements.
The structure of compounds often shows covalent bonding character.
In everyday life, think about cleaning supplies containing acids.

items: Toilet bowl cleaner uses strong acids.

draw.text: Real Life: Acid strength in cleaners

faq.q: What determines if an oxoacid is strong or weak?
faq.a: The strength of an oxoacid generally increases with the oxidation state of the central atom and the number of oxygen atoms bonded to it.
asks: How do I predict acid strength?
Does more oxygen mean stronger acid?

faq.q: How does electronegativity change across the p-block?
faq.a: Electronegativity generally increases from left to right across a period, becoming highest for the halogens in Group 17.
asks: Which element is most electronegative here?

faq.q: Are all p-block elements always highly reactive?
faq.a: Reactivity varies greatly; for instance, Group 18 elements are very stable and unreactive due to a full valence shell.

faq.q: What is the difference between a halide and an oxoacid?
faq.a: A halide is a compound containing a halogen, like $\text{NaCl}$, while an oxoacid contains oxygen atoms bonded to a central atom, like $\text{HNO}3$.
asks: What do they have in common?

faq.q: Does the size of the atom affect its acidity?
faq.a: Yes, larger atoms can sometimes stabilize the conjugate base, which affects the acid's strength in complex ways.
asks: Does atomic size matter for acid strength?
Is there a direct link between size and acidity?

facts: Electronegativity generally increases across a period from left to right.
Oxoacid strength increases with the oxidation state of the central element.
Group 18 elements are known for their chemical inertness.

quiz.say: Which element in Group 17 has the highest electronegativity?
quiz.why: Fluorine is the most electronegative element in the entire periodic table.

wrong.1: Chlorine is also highly electronegative, but fluorine is higher.
wrong.2: Oxygen is in a different group, not Group 17.
wrong.3: Bromine is less electronegative than fluorine.

quiz.say: When comparing $\text{H}2\text{S}$ and $\text{H}2\text{SO}4$, which is the stronger acid?
quiz.why: The acidity increases significantly when the central atom's oxidation state and oxygen content increase.

wrong.1: Hydrogen sulfide is a weak acid compared to strong oxoacids.
wrong.2: Acid strength depends on multiple factors, not just the presence of hydrogen.
wrong.3: The number of hydrogen atoms does not determine the acid strength.

quiz.say: If you move from Group 13 to Group 18, what generally happens to the metallic character?
quiz.why: As you move across the p-block, the elements become less metallic and more nonmetallic.

wrong.0: The trend is generally monotonic across the period.
wrong.2: Metallic character decreases because the atoms hold onto their valence electrons more tightly.
wrong.3: The chemical nature changes significantly across the groups.
